question.text: The Ming dynasty was established after the Red Turban rebellions that overthrew this Chinese successor dynasty to the Mongol Empire. Marco Polo's writings about China were during the time of this dynasty.
question.answerHtml: Yuan Dynasty [do not accept or prompt on "Mongol Dynasty"]
question.clue: It established its capital at Cambaluc , now modern day Beijing.

swap.text: This economic and social campaign beginning in 1958 sought to rapidly transform China from an agrarian economy to modern communist society. It failed miserably.
swap.clue: This period grew out of a conference in the resort city of Qingdao and the Anti-Rightist Campaign.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Chinese history.
question.text: This rebellion's leader, Hong Xiuquan, claimed to be the brother of Jesus, and it attempted to establish a "Heavenly Kingdom" in mid-nineteenth century China.
question.clue: Major ethnic groups that participated in this rebellion were the Zhuang and the Hakka.

swap.text: The UK turned over control of this Special Administrative Region to China in 1997, two years beforePortugal did the same with nearby Macau.
swap.clue: A series of protests in this city was named after the umbrellas used to shield demonstrators from police tear gas.

question.text: Japanese leader Toyotomi Hideyoshi invaded Joseon as a stepping stone to attacking this Chinese dynasty. This dynasty was founded by the Hongwu ["hohng-woo"] Emperor after he won the Battle of Lake Poyang ["p'woh-yong"].
question.clue: General Wu Sangui's opening of Shanhai Pass ended this dynasty, which was crushed at the battle of Songjin.

swap.leadin: This dynasty's capital of Kaifeng (kai-FUHNG) was sacked by the Jurchen in the Jingkang incident, forcing this dynasty to move its capital to Hangzhou (haang-JOH).
swap.text: Name this dynasty, which ruled China from 960 to 1279 CᐧE. It was conquered by Kublai Khan and succeeded by the Yuan Dynasty.
swap.clue: Bi Sheng worked under this dynasty, which switched lines of succession due to the Jingkang Incident.

question.text: During the war, Chiang's Kuomintang forces chased the retreating communists all the way north to Shaanxi in this military campaign, during which Mao Zedong came to power.
question.clue: The Fifth Encirclement forced this event, which Otto Braun took part in. The participants of this event defeated warlord forces at the Battle of Luding Bridge and reshuffled their leadership at the Zunyi Conference.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about a Chinese dynasty.
swap.text: The Tang golden age was brought to an end by this rebellion named for its leader, an ex-Tang general, who established the rival Yan Dynasty with his lieutenant Shi Siming. It was one of the costliest wars in human history.
swap.clue: This event began with the siege of Luoyang, and later saw the capture of the capital, Chang'an.

question.leadin: This dynasty defeated its predecessor at the Battle of Muye, capturing its capital at modern Anyang.
question.text: Name this longest ruling Chinese dynasty who thereafter became the first to claim a "Mandate of Heaven" for their rule.
question.clue: The Hundred Schools flourished during the Eastern part of the dynasty, whose rulers were the first to claim the (* ) Mandate of Heaven.

swap.leadin: Name these famous women married to famous men.
swap.text: This third wife of Mao Zedong was a deputy leader of the Cultural Revolution before being ousted in 1976 as one of the Gang of Four.
swap.clue: This person was the main target of a protest that flouted a ban on mourning called the "Five Nos".

question.leadin: The yin privilege allowed high ranking bureaucrats to place their sons into low positions of power without having to deal with this system.
question.text: Name this system, success in which allowed scholar-bureaucrats to advance by demonstrating knowledge of wenxue. The challenging Eight-legged essay was an integral part of this system.
question.answerHtml: Chinese imperial examinations [accept equivalents like the Chinese civil service exams]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about writing in historical China.
swap.text: This Han dynasty official chronicled the history China up to Empress Wu in his Records of the Grand Historian.
swap.clue: This court eunuch wrote a biography of emperors starting with Huangdi, also known as the Yellow Emperor, to his contemporary Emperor Wu of Han.

question.leadin: This state gained power thanks to Shang Yang's reforms, and the kingdom of Han instantly surrendered to this kingdom when King An believed they would invade.
question.text: Name this kingdom whose leader Ying Zheng conquered six other states, which began a namesake dynasty.
question.clue: Despite claims in Records of the Grand Historian, this dynasty most likely did not "bury the Confucians" during a book burning.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Chinese civil wars.
swap.text: This Turkic general launched a rebellion against the Tang and created the short-lived Yan Dynasty. This rebellion led to the execution of Yang Guifei, one of the four great beauties of Ancient China.
swap.clue: After Li's death precipitated a power struggle, this man declared the Yen Dynasty.

question.leadin: A racist myth about these people claims a merchant named Wu Feng sacrificed himself to a beheading to persuade these people to stop head-hunting.
question.text: Give this broad class of people including the Bunun, Puyuma, and Atayal, who were taught baseball by the Japanese. When Koxinga came to their country, some of these people fought with him against the Dutch.
question.clue: Chiang Kai-Shek's "make mountains like plains" movement attempted to promote Mandarin and nationalism among these people.

swap.text: Mitsuomi Kamio was ordered to take this Chinese city from German control following the entry of Japan in WWI. The siege of this city laid the groundwork for the Japanese expanding their influence in China.
swap.clue: During World War I, Japan captured this city in Germany's Kiautschou Bay Concession. This Chinese city is home to St. Michael's Cathedral, built by German missionaries.

question.text: An Lushan was assassinated by one of these people who An had made a eunuch. These people, who ruled the Liao Dynasty, founded a "black" state after a Jurchen invasion in 1124 forced them to flee to Central Asia.
question.clue: The Goryeo Dynasty engaged in a series of wars with these Mongol barbarians. Ruled by the Liao Dynasty, they were based out of Manchuria and launched three major invasions of Korea.

swap.leadin: This dynasty's Xiaowen [SHYOW-wun] Emperor and Dowager Empress Feng [fung] devised a system in which all land would be owned by the government and given out based on family size for the length of a farmer's life.
swap.text: Name this dynasty that unified the "Sixteen Kingdoms" of the Five Barbarians to found the first of the Northern Dynasties. This dynasty enacted mandatory Sinicization policies for its own elite under Xianwen [SHYEHN-wun].
swap.answerHtml: Northern Wèi [or Tuòbá Wei or Later Wèi or Yuán Wèi; accept Xiānbēi [shyehn bay]]

question.text: Stories of widows from the Local History of Tancheng are a source of this author's microhistory The Death of Woman Wang. This historian wrote The Memory Palace of Matteo Ricci and The Search for Modern China.

swap.text: The Five Dynasties era came to an end with the establishment of this dynasty, which survived until 1127 as its Nan or Southern version until overrun by the Mongols.
swap.clue: A branch of this dynasty was noted for the beauty of its capital at Kaifeng.
